moves.headline: Micron surges 19% as chip stocks rebound on Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia
moves.summary: Micron rose 19.0% to $707.70 on heavy volume as memory and chip stocks recovered from the previous week’s rout. Nvidia’s decision to reinstate Jensen Huang lifted the whole AI supply chain, and Citi argued that worries about AI infrastructure spending were overdone.
why: Micron had fallen sharply with the rest of the semiconductor sector the week before, as leadership turmoil at Nvidia, a reported SEC probe and doubts about the financing of AI data centres hit every company that supplies them. Memory makers were among the hardest hit because their earnings depend on high-bandwidth memory sold into AI servers.

There was no company-specific news. The move was a rebound with the sector: Nvidia’s board reinstating Huang removed the most visible risk to AI demand, and commentary from Citi suggesting that the fears about infrastructure spending were overblown gave memory stocks extra support.
context: US stocks had their best day since April 2025 on November 23. The Nasdaq rose close to 7% during the session and the S&P 500 about 5%, recovering much of the previous week’s sell-off, in which chip stocks had their worst week since 2001.
More than 120 US companies worth over $2 billion rose 10% or more on the day, almost all of them chipmakers, memory makers, data-centre suppliers and other AI-linked stocks.

moves.headline: Micron drops 14% as memory stocks lead the semiconductor crash
moves.summary: Micron shares fell 13.9% to $594.51 as the AI sell-off hit memory makers hardest, alongside Sandisk, Western Digital and Seagate. There was no company-specific news; investors sold the stocks that had gained most from the AI-driven memory shortage.
why: Micron was among the biggest beneficiaries of the AI boom in 2026: a global shortage of high-bandwidth and conventional memory drove prices and profits to records, and the stock rose many times over. That made it one of the most exposed stocks when investors began to question how long AI infrastructure spending can continue at its current pace. Midday reports on November 20 attributed Micron’s fall to growing concern about chip valuations and the outlook for the sector rather than any change in its own business.
The memory group fell together: Sandisk dropped 16%, Western Digital 12% and Seagate 12% on the same day. Over the week Micron lost more than 20%, as did Nvidia, Marvell, Nebius and CoreWeave.
context: On November 20 the Nasdaq Composite fell 5.3% and the S&P 500 3.7%, pushing the S&P 500 and the Dow into correction territory and wiping out the Nasdaq’s gain for 2026. Semiconductors led the fall, capping their worst week since 2001.

Memory is the most cyclical part of the chip industry. Investors who remember how quickly memory prices collapsed in 2019 and 2023 tend to sell first when demand forecasts are questioned, even when current results are strong.
